The purpose of PROSIX is to reach the optimal level of composites usage in every single project.

VYRONIS Technologies Ltd
Sector: Space Biotech • AI & Radiation Biology • Astronaut Health
Location: Glasgow, Scotland
Founder: Varun Cruz
Overview 
VYRONIS Technologies is a space biotechnology company developing radiation-adaptive bio-AI systems to enhance astronaut health, radiation resilience, and biological safety in deep-space missions. The company’s flagship platform, GENORA™, integrates radiobiological data, molecular AI, and predictive genomics to model how living systems adapt to ionising radiation; enabling early detection, intervention, and countermeasure design for spaceflight and nuclear medicine environments. 
ESA BIC Focus 
Through the ESA Business Incubation Centre UK, VYRONIS is advancing the GENORA™ Translational Framework (TRL 3–7) — combining laboratory data, in-silico simulations, and microgravity-exposed biological datasets. The aim is to produce adaptive bio-AI algorithms that can predict and mitigate radiation damage for astronauts, satellites, and terrestrial healthcare systems. Vision To pioneer a new era of bio-adaptive intelligence for human space exploration — ensuring every mission beyond Earth is powered by biologically informed, AI-driven health resilience. Applications Space Health: Predictive modelling for astronaut exposure and countermeasure optimisation. Terrestrial Medicine: Radiotherapy safety, oncology insights, and emergency-response biotechnologies. Dual-Use AI Systems: Algorithms for defence, nuclear energy, and planetary colonisation research. 
Key Partners 
ESA BIC UK (incubation support) 
Innovate UK (funding) 
Academic collaborations with UK and EU research institutions

Robody Cares is a new type of ambulatory care service where local nursing staff perform some visits to patients in person and some via remote-operated, humanoid robots – “Robodies”. This provides protection and assistance to the patient 24/7 while the patient maintains personal contact with people in their community.
With an aging population and families more distant than ever, we are sleep walking into a care crisis. This new challenge needs a new solution – Robody Cares – that combines the benefits of modern technology with human care, ensuring that your loved ones are always well taken care of and receive the help they need.
Combining AI, AR, and 5G, Robodies are human robotic avatars allowing its operator to teleport their senses, action, and presence anywhere on the planet or in space. This makes Robodies an alternative for space based operations in the future.

description:
SI Robotics is a Warsaw-based deep-tech company developing sovereign European humanoid and robotic systems for industrial, defence, and space applications. We are a Physical-AI-first company, integrating advanced actuators, tendon-based joints, and compliant control systems with reinforcement-learning frameworks to create embodied intelligence for the physical world.

Our mission is to advance Physical AI — the fusion of mechanical design, sensing, and neural control that allows robots to understand, interact with, and adapt to their environment with human-like precision. We believe this domain will define the next generation of autonomy across terrestrial and orbital contexts.

Within the space sector, SI Robotics develops lightweight, ECSS-compliant actuator systems for robotic arms, EVA/IVA assistance, and on-orbit servicing. Our modular joint architecture and torque-controlled drives are designed to operate under the mechanical, radiation, and thermal constraints of space environments.

We are fully aligned with European AI, data, and machinery regulations (including the 2027 AI Act and Machinery Regulation). SI Robotics’ architecture ensures full traceability, explainability, and data sovereignty, making our Physical AI stack natively compliant with EU ethical and legal frameworks — a key differentiator from non-EU robotics providers.

SI Robotics contributes to the emerging European Physical AI policy agenda, supporting ESA and the European Commission in building safe, transparent, and sovereign autonomy for robotic systems. We work closely with research institutions and industrial partners to develop embodied AI models that meet dual-use and security-sensitive requirements, ensuring resilience and interoperability across ESA, defence, and industry ecosystems.
